## You're the land manager

Forget doctors and biopsies — every other DCA tutorial uses them, and they get in
the way. Here's the situation instead.

A **rare plant** on land you manage has **8 known effective populations**. Under
the listing rules, if there are **fewer than 12** effective populations it gets
**listed** — which lands you with roughly **\$60,000 in consulting fees** (plus a
pile of new restrictions). You're fairly sure more populations are out there: you
have a **species distribution model (SDM)** that scores all **500 candidate
habitat sites** across your unit with a probability of occurrence. But the plant
is *rare* — only about **2%** of sites are actually occupied, so that's roughly
**10 undiscovered populations hidden among 500 sites.**

You have one lever: a **seasonal field crew**. Two people, two weeks, already on
the payroll — about **\$6,400** of their time (40 hrs × \$20 × 2 for fringe × 2
people × 2 weeks). Realistically they can carefully survey about **30 sites**.

> **The decision: where do you send them?** Find **4 more** occupied sites and you
> reach 12, and the listing — and its \$60K — goes away.

You have three ways to choose which sites to survey:

- <span class="chip chip-all"></span> **Survey every site** — impossible here (500
  sites, a crew that can do 30), and the formal version is a disaster at 2%
  occupancy, as you'll see.
- <span class="chip chip-none"></span> **Survey nothing** — free, but you stay at 8
  populations and eat the \$60K listing.
- <span class="chip chip-model"></span> **Use the model** — send the crew to the
  sites the SDM is most confident about.

**Decision curve analysis** scores these on a common currency — **net benefit** —
and then we'll translate that straight into *populations found* and *dollars*.

## The one idea you need: the threshold probability

How confident does the model have to be before a site is worth a crew-day? That
cutoff is the **threshold probability**, $p_t$. It isn't a statistic — it's a
statement about *your* costs:

$$\frac{p_t}{1 - p_t} = \frac{\text{cost of one wasted survey}}{\text{value of one occupied site found}}$$

Set $p_t$ low and you're saying *"I'll check even a long shot"*; set it high and
you'll only spend a crew-day on near-sure things. **There's no single correct
threshold** — DCA's trick is to evaluate *every* threshold at once and let you see
where using the model actually pays.

## Net benefit

For any strategy, at a chosen threshold $p_t$:

::: {.formula}
$$\text{Net benefit} = \underbrace{\frac{\text{occupied sites found}}{n}}_{\text{the good}} \;-\; \underbrace{\frac{\text{empty sites surveyed}}{n} \times \frac{p_t}{1 - p_t}}_{\text{the cost of wasted trips}}$$
:::

Net benefit is "occupied sites found per site surveyed," after subtracting a
penalty for wasted trips weighted by *your* cost ratio. "Survey nothing" always
scores exactly **0** — the natural baseline. At 2% prevalence these per-site
numbers get tiny and abstract (you'll see net benefits like 0.005), which is
exactly why the panel below **translates them into populations and dollars.**

## The interactive part {#widget}

Drag the sliders. The left chart is the classic DCA curve (net benefit vs. every
threshold); the right chart and the tiles turn your selected threshold into the
decision you actually face.

::: {.widget}

Everything is simulated in your browser. <strong>AUC-PR</strong> (area under the

## How to read it — and the real lesson

- **Left (DCA) chart.** Where the <span class="chip chip-model"></span> model line
  is highest, using the model beats both naive rules. Notice the
  <span class="chip chip-all"></span> "survey every site" line starts at the
  prevalence (~2%) on the far left and then *plummets* — at 2% occupancy,
  surveying everything is almost all wasted trips. The
  <span class="chip chip-none"></span> zero line is "survey nothing."
- **Right chart.** The payoff: your probability of finding the 4 populations you
  need. **Model-guided vs. random is the difference between ~0% and nearly
  certain.** A good SDM here isn't a nicety — it's the whole ballgame.
- **The non-obvious bit.** Your crew is *already paid for the season*, so a wasted
  trip costs you almost nothing extra — which means the net-benefit-optimal
  threshold is **low**. Start at $p_t = 0.45$ and the model flags only a handful of
  sites, leaving most of your crew's time unused. **Slide the threshold down** and
  watch P(avoid listing) climb as you put the whole crew to work on the model's
  best bets. That's DCA telling you to be *less* picky than instinct says, because
  your costs are sunk.

Try it: push **AUC-PR** down toward 0.2 (a weak model) and the model's edge over
random collapses. Push crew **capacity** up and watch how much more a bigger crew
buys you.

## Why this beats "my AUC-PR is 0.7"

A skill metric describes the *model*. Net benefit — and its translation into
populations and dollars — describes *the decision you make with it*, at the cost
trade-off you actually face. Two models with identical AUC-PR can lead to very
different outcomes once capacity, prevalence, and stakes enter. The gap between a
good model and a *useful decision* is exactly what decision curve analysis makes
visible.

# §2 · A fair baseline: beating the expert

§1 had a dirty secret. I pitted the model against *random* deployment — and no
field botanist searches at random. That strawman is exactly why the model looked
like a savior (0% → 98%). The honest question in decision curve analysis is always
**"does the model beat the realistic status quo?"** — and here the status quo is a
knowledgeable botanist. In DCA terms, the expert's shortlist is just **another
strategy whose curve we plot**; the model's value is how far it sits *above the
expert's line*, not above random.

**Two biological layers matter here.** Your SDM is good at predicting *suitable
habitat* (a realistic **AUC-PR ≈ 0.70**). But suitable ≠ occupied: whether a
suitable site actually holds a population is a colonization lottery — dispersal,
history, microsite. That second layer is nearly random, and it puts a hard
**ceiling** on *anyone's* ability to find populations. In this landscape even a
*perfect* habitat model, surveying 30 sites, has only about a **48% chance** of
finding the 4 populations you need. That ceiling is why a botanist who gets **40%
of populations onto a 50-site shortlist is almost god-like** — they're already
near the limit of what's knowable.

So two readers — the SDM and the expert — each squint at the same hidden
suitability through their own noise. The expert catches ~40% of populations; the
question is what the model *adds*.

**And this time, no guessing the threshold.** The slider for $p_t$ is gone. You set
the *costs* — what a wasted survey costs, and what the listing costs — and the
widget **derives** $p_t$ from them (plus your capacity). You set dollars; the math
sets the probability.

::: {.widget}

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
```

## How to read §2

- **Left chart.** The <span class="chip chip-model"></span> SDM's net-benefit curve
  vs. the <span class="chip chip-all"></span> expert's shortlist (a fixed strategy,
  so a straight line). The black line is the **derived threshold** — you no longer
  pick it. Where the SDM curve sits *above* the expert line at that threshold, the
  model earns its keep; where they touch, it doesn't.
- **Right chart.** Probability of actually finding the 4 populations, for the expert
  alone, the SDM alone, and **both combined** — against the dashed **ceiling** (the
  best any method could do). Notice how little daylight there is between a good SDM
  and a good expert, and how the *combination* reaches closest to the ceiling:
  because the model and the botanist make **independent** errors about the same
  habitat, averaging them cancels noise. **That — not replacing the expert — is
  where the model's honest value lives.**
- **The humbling part.** Everything is pinned under ~48%. When occupancy is a
  colonization lottery, no amount of model skill makes the problem easy; it only
  moves you a few points. DCA is what keeps you honest about how few.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// ---------- math helpers ----------
normPDF = (x) => Math.exp(-0.5 * x * x) / Math.sqrt(2 * Math.PI)

function normCDF(x) {
  const t = 1 / (1 + 0.2316419 * Math.abs(x));
  const d = normPDF(x);
  let p = d * t * (0.319381530 + t * (-0.356563782 + t * (1.781477937 +
            t * (-1.821255978 + t * 1.330274429))));
  return x >= 0 ? 1 - p : p;
}

// calibrated posterior P(occupied | latent score x), bi-normal model
posterior = (x, mu, prev) => {
  const fP = prev * normPDF(x - mu);
  const fA = (1 - prev) * normPDF(x);
  return fP / (fP + fA);
}

// analytic PR-AUC for a bi-normal model with separation mu and prevalence prev
function prAUC(mu, prev) {
  let prevR = 0, prevP = 1, area = 0;
  for (let c = 7; c >= -7.0001; c -= 0.01) {
    const tpr = 1 - normCDF(c - mu);           // recall
    const fpr = 1 - normCDF(c);
    const tp = prev * tpr, fp = (1 - prev) * fpr;
    const prec = (tp + fp) > 0 ? tp / (tp + fp) : 1;
    area += (tpr - prevR) * (prec + prevP) / 2;
    prevR = tpr; prevP = prec;
  }
  return area;
}

// invert PR-AUC -> separation mu (binary search) at a given prevalence
function muForPRAUC(target, prev) {
  if (target <= prev) return 0;
  let lo = 0, hi = 8;
  for (let k = 0; k < 50; k++) {
    const mid = (lo + hi) / 2;
    if (prAUC(mid, prev) < target) lo = mid; else hi = mid;
  }
  return (lo + hi) / 2;
}

// seeded RNG
function mulberry32(seed) {
  let a = seed >>> 0;
  return function () {
    a |= 0; a = (a + 0x6D2B79F5) | 0;
    let t = Math.imul(a ^ (a >>> 15), 1 | a);
    t = (t + Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 7), 61 | t)) ^ t;
    return ((t ^ (t >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296;
  };
}

// linear interpolation into a (grid, values) table
function interp(grid, arr, x) {
  if (x <= grid[0]) return arr[0];
  if (x >= grid[grid.length - 1]) return arr[arr.length - 1];
  const i = d3.bisectLeft(grid, x);
  const t = (x - grid[i - 1]) / (grid[i] - grid[i - 1]);
  return arr[i - 1] * (1 - t) + arr[i] * t;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// ---------- fixed scenario constants ----------
M = 500            // candidate sites scored by the SDM
KNOWN = 8          // known populations now
TARGET = 12        // threshold for avoiding listing
NEED = TARGET - KNOWN   // = 4 more needed
LISTING = 60000    // $ cost if listed
CREW = 6400        // $ cost of deploying the crew
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
mu = muForPRAUC(prauc, prev)

// ---------- analytic DCA net-benefit curves (smooth) ----------
// score cutoff c such that posterior(c) = pt  (monotone increasing in x)
function scoreCutoff(ptv, mu, prev) {
  if (mu <= 0) return ptv <= prev ? -Infinity : Infinity;
  let lo = -20, hi = 30;
  for (let k = 0; k < 60; k++) {
    const mid = (lo + hi) / 2;
    if (posterior(mid, mu, prev) < ptv) lo = mid; else hi = mid;
  }
  return (lo + hi) / 2;
}
function nbModel(ptv) {
  const c = scoreCutoff(ptv, mu, prev);
  const sens = 1 - normCDF(c - mu);           // P(flag | occupied)
  const fpr  = 1 - normCDF(c);                // P(flag | empty)
  return prev * sens - (1 - prev) * fpr * (ptv / (1 - ptv));
}
function nbAll(ptv) {
  return prev - (1 - prev) * (ptv / (1 - ptv));
}
nbGrid = d3.range(0.02, 0.8001, 0.01)
nbData = nbGrid.flatMap(t => [
  { threshold: t, nb: nbModel(t), strategy: "Use the model" },
  { threshold: t, nb: nbAll(t),   strategy: "Survey every site" }
])
nbMax = d3.max(nbGrid, t => nbModel(t))
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// ---------- Monte Carlo over simulated field seasons ----------
// For each threshold: dispatch the crew to the highest-probability flagged sites
// (capped at capacity), count occupied sites found, score P(found >= NEED).
scenario = {
  const R = 1500;
  const rng = mulberry32(777);
  const gauss = () => {
    const u1 = rng(), u2 = rng();
    return Math.sqrt(-2 * Math.log(u1 + 1e-12)) * Math.cos(2 * Math.PI * u2);
  };
  const grid = d3.range(0.02, 0.8001, 0.02);
  const emModel = grid.map(() => 0), winModel = grid.map(() => 0);
  let emTop = 0, winTop = 0, emRand = 0, winRand = 0;

  for (let r = 0; r < R; r++) {
    const ys = new Int8Array(M), ps = new Float64Array(M);
    for (let i = 0; i < M; i++) {
      const y = rng() < prev ? 1 : 0;
      const x = (y ? mu : 0) + gauss();
      ys[i] = y; ps[i] = posterior(x, mu, prev);
    }
    const order = Array.from({ length: M }, (_, i) => i).sort((a, b) => ps[b] - ps[a]);
    const prefY = new Int16Array(M + 1);
    for (let i = 0; i < M; i++) prefY[i + 1] = prefY[i] + ys[order[i]];

    // use-the-model, full capacity (top-K, threshold-independent)
    const fTop = prefY[Math.min(capacity, M)];
    emTop += fTop; if (fTop >= NEED) winTop++;

    // random capacity sites
    const idx = Array.from({ length: M }, (_, i) => i);
    let fR = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < capacity; i++) {
      const j = i + Math.floor(rng() * (M - i));
      const tmp = idx[i]; idx[i] = idx[j]; idx[j] = tmp;
      fR += ys[idx[i]];
    }
    emRand += fR; if (fR >= NEED) winRand++;

    // model with threshold pt (flag p>=pt, survey highest-prob up to capacity)
    for (let g = 0; g < grid.length; g++) {
      const t = grid[g];
      let lo = 0, hi = M;                         // count of ps>=t (order is desc)
      while (lo < hi) { const mid = (lo + hi) >> 1; if (ps[order[mid]] >= t) lo = mid + 1; else hi = mid; }
      const surveyed = Math.min(lo, capacity);
      const f = prefY[surveyed];
      emModel[g] += f; if (f >= NEED) winModel[g]++;
    }
  }
  return {
    R, grid,
    emModel: emModel.map(v => v / R),
    pwinModel: winModel.map(v => v / R),
    emTop: emTop / R, pwinTop: winTop / R,
    emRand: emRand / R, pwinRand: winRand / R
  };
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// values at the currently selected threshold
cutoff = scoreCutoff(pt, mu, prev)
sensPt = 1 - normCDF(cutoff - mu)
fprPt  = 1 - normCDF(cutoff)
nFlag  = Math.round(M * (prev * sensPt + (1 - prev) * fprPt))   // sites flagged at pt
nSurvey = Math.min(nFlag, capacity)
expFinds = interp(scenario.grid, scenario.emModel, pt)
pWin     = interp(scenario.grid, scenario.pwinModel, pt)
dollarsModel = pWin * LISTING - CREW         // expected savings vs doing nothing
dollarsRand  = scenario.pwinRand * LISTING - CREW
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// ---------- plain-language verdict ----------
verdictBox = {
  let cls, msg;
  const idle = capacity - nSurvey;
  if (pWin >= 0.75) {
    cls = "win";
    msg = html`At <b>pₜ = ${(pt*100).toFixed(0)}%</b> with an AUC-PR of
      <b>${prauc.toFixed(2)}</b>, the model-guided crew has a <b>${(pWin*100).toFixed(0)}%
      chance</b> of finding the ${NEED} populations you need — expected value
      <b>${money(dollarsModel)}</b> versus doing nothing. A random crew's odds here
      are ${(scenario.pwinRand*100).toFixed(0)}%. The model is doing the work.`;
  } else if (pWin >= 0.35) {
    cls = "tie";
    msg = html`At <b>pₜ = ${(pt*100).toFixed(0)}%</b> you've a <b>${(pWin*100).toFixed(0)}%</b>
      shot — decent, but you're ${idle > 0 ? html`flagging only ${nFlag} sites and leaving
      <b>${idle} crew-days idle</b>. Your crew is already paid for the season, so a
      wasted trip costs almost nothing — <b>slide pₜ down</b> to put the whole crew
      to work and watch the odds climb.` : html`leaving odds on the table — try a
      stronger model or a bigger crew.`}`;
  } else {
    cls = "lose";
    msg = html`At <b>pₜ = ${(pt*100).toFixed(0)}%</b> the odds of avoiding listing are only
      <b>${(pWin*100).toFixed(0)}%</b>. ${idle > 0 ? html`You're flagging just ${nFlag}
      sites while your crew could do ${capacity} — <b>lower the threshold</b> to use that
      capacity.` : html`Even at full tilt this model + crew can't reliably clear the bar;
      a better SDM or more survey capacity is the fix.`}`;
  }
  return htl.html`<div class="verdict ${cls}">${msg}</div>`;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// ===================== §2 : expert baseline =====================
// inverse standard normal (Acklam) — not needed in §1, add here
function normInv(p) {
  const a = [-3.969683028665376e+01, 2.209460984245205e+02, -2.759285104469687e+02,
             1.383577518672690e+02, -3.066479806614716e+01, 2.506628277459239e+00];
  const b = [-5.447609879822406e+01, 1.615858368580409e+02, -1.556989798598866e+02,
             6.680131188771972e+01, -1.328068155288572e+01];
  const c = [-7.784894002430293e-03, -3.223964580411365e-01, -2.400758277161838e+00,
             -2.549732539343734e+00, 4.374664141464968e+00, 2.938163982698783e+00];
  const d = [7.784695709041462e-03, 3.224671290700398e-01, 2.445134137142996e+00,
             3.754408661907416e+00];
  const plow = 0.02425, phigh = 1 - plow;
  let q, r;
  if (p < plow) { q = Math.sqrt(-2 * Math.log(p));
    return (((((c[0]*q+c[1])*q+c[2])*q+c[3])*q+c[4])*q+c[5]) / ((((d[0]*q+d[1])*q+d[2])*q+d[3])*q+1);
  } else if (p <= phigh) { q = p - 0.5; r = q * q;
    return (((((a[0]*r+a[1])*r+a[2])*r+a[3])*r+a[4])*r+a[5])*q / (((((b[0]*r+b[1])*r+b[2])*r+b[3])*r+b[4])*r+1);
  } else { q = Math.sqrt(-2 * Math.log(1 - p));
    return -(((((c[0]*q+c[1])*q+c[2])*q+c[3])*q+c[4])*q+c[5]) / ((((d[0]*q+d[1])*q+d[2])*q+d[3])*q+1);
  }
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// two-layer model constants (prevalence fixed at 2%)
BETA = 0.6                                   // suitability -> occupancy coupling (weak = hard ceiling)
ALPHA2 = normInv(0.02) * Math.sqrt(1 + BETA * BETA)   // so E[occupancy] = 2%
SHORT2 = 50                                  // expert shortlist size
SE2 = 0.644                                  // expert noise -> ~40% population recall@50 (calibrated offline)

// AUC-PR(suitability) <-> model noise sigma_m, precomputed offline
SIGMA_LUT = [0.10,0.20,0.30,0.40,0.50,0.60,0.75,0.90,1.10,1.35,1.65,2.00,2.50]
AUCPR_LUT = [0.9856,0.9472,0.8923,0.8280,0.7606,0.6942,0.6026,0.5240,0.4400,0.3631,0.3002,0.2524,0.2106]

function sigmaFromAUC(target) {
  const A = AUCPR_LUT, S = SIGMA_LUT;
  if (target >= A[0]) return S[0];
  if (target <= A[A.length - 1]) return S[S.length - 1];
  for (let i = 0; i < A.length - 1; i++) {
    if (target <= A[i] && target >= A[i + 1]) {
      const t = (A[i] - target) / (A[i] - A[i + 1]);
      return S[i] + t * (S[i + 1] - S[i]);
    }
  }
  return S[S.length - 1];
}

// calibrated occupancy posterior given model score m
function postM2(m, sm) {
  const vp = sm * sm / (1 + sm * sm), mp = m / (1 + sm * sm);
  return normCDF((BETA * mp + ALPHA2) / Math.sqrt(1 + BETA * BETA * vp));
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Monte Carlo over field seasons: expert vs SDM vs combined, plus net-benefit curves
scenario2 = {
  const sm = sigmaFromAUC(prauc2), se = SE2, cap = capacity2, R = 1200;
  const rng = mulberry32(2024);
  const gauss = () => { const u1 = rng(), u2 = rng();
    return Math.sqrt(-2 * Math.log(u1 + 1e-12)) * Math.cos(2 * Math.PI * u2); };
  const grid = d3.range(0.005, 0.3001, 0.005);
  const G = grid.length;
  const diffTP = new Float64Array(G + 1), diffFP = new Float64Array(G + 1);
  const wM = 1 / (sm * sm), wE = 1 / (se * se);
  let TPe = 0, FPe = 0, winE = 0, winM = 0, winC = 0, winCeil = 0, p30 = 0;
  const nTot = R * M;

  for (let r = 0; r < R; r++) {
    const H = new Float64Array(M), Y = new Int8Array(M), Ms = new Float64Array(M), Es = new Float64Array(M);
    for (let i = 0; i < M; i++) {
      const h = gauss(); H[i] = h;
      Y[i] = rng() < normCDF(BETA * h + ALPHA2) ? 1 : 0;
      Ms[i] = h + sm * gauss(); Es[i] = h + se * gauss();
    }
    // SDM net-benefit curve: flag p̂ >= pt over ALL sites (difference-array trick)
    for (let i = 0; i < M; i++) {
      const pv = postM2(Ms[i], sm);
      let lo = 0, hi = G; while (lo < hi) { const mid = (lo + hi) >> 1; if (grid[mid] <= pv) lo = mid + 1; else hi = mid; }
      if (Y[i]) { diffTP[0] += 1; diffTP[lo] -= 1; } else { diffFP[0] += 1; diffFP[lo] -= 1; }
    }
    // rank by each reader
    const ix = Array.from({ length: M }, (_, i) => i);
    const idxM = ix.slice().sort((a, b) => Ms[b] - Ms[a]);
    const idxE = ix.slice().sort((a, b) => Es[b] - Es[a]);
    const idxC = ix.slice().sort((a, b) => (Ms[b]*wM + Es[b]*wE) - (Ms[a]*wM + Es[a]*wE));
    const idxH = ix.slice().sort((a, b) => H[b] - H[a]);
    let fE = 0, fM = 0, fC = 0, fH = 0;
    for (let k = 0; k < cap; k++) { fE += Y[idxE[k]]; fM += Y[idxM[k]]; fC += Y[idxC[k]]; fH += Y[idxH[k]]; }
    TPe += fE; FPe += (cap - fE);
    if (fE >= NEED) winE++; if (fM >= NEED) winM++; if (fC >= NEED) winC++; if (fH >= NEED) winCeil++;
    p30 += postM2(Ms[idxM[cap - 1]], sm);
  }
  let aTP = 0, aFP = 0;
  const nbM = [], nbE = [];
  for (let g = 0; g < G; g++) {
    aTP += diffTP[g]; aFP += diffFP[g];
    const w = grid[g] / (1 - grid[g]);
    nbM.push((aTP - aFP * w) / nTot);
    nbE.push((TPe - FPe * w) / nTot);
  }
  return { grid, nbM, nbE, pE: winE/R, pM: winM/R, pC: winC/R, pCeil: winCeil/R, p30: p30/R, cap, sm };
}
```

```{ojs}
// derived threshold from costs + capacity
Vfind2 = listcost / NEED                         // value of one find (listing cost spread over the 4 needed)
ptCost = cwaste / (cwaste + Vfind2)              // "worth-it" floor
ptCap = scenario2.p30                            // posterior of the marginal (capacity-th) site
ptOp = Math.max(ptCost, ptCap)                   // operating threshold
ptBinds = ptCost >= ptCap ? "cost" : "capacity"
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
verdict2 = {
  const edgeM = (scenario2.pM - scenario2.pE) * 100;
  const edgeC = (scenario2.pC - scenario2.pE) * 100;
  let cls, msg;
  if (edgeM >= 8) {
    cls = "win";
    msg = html`At AUC-PR <b>${prauc2.toFixed(2)}</b> the SDM beats even a god-like expert
      by <b>${edgeM.toFixed(0)} points</b> of listing-avoidance (${(scenario2.pM*100).toFixed(0)}%
      vs ${(scenario2.pE*100).toFixed(0)}%). Combining the two reaches
      <b>${(scenario2.pC*100).toFixed(0)}%</b>, close to the ${(scenario2.pCeil*100).toFixed(0)}% ceiling.`;
  } else if (edgeM >= -2) {
    cls = "tie";
    msg = html`At AUC-PR <b>${prauc2.toFixed(2)}</b> the SDM is <b>barely distinguishable</b> from a
      god-like expert (${(scenario2.pM*100).toFixed(0)}% vs ${(scenario2.pE*100).toFixed(0)}%) —
      both are pinned near the <b>${(scenario2.pCeil*100).toFixed(0)}% biological ceiling</b>.
      The model's honest value shows up in the <b>combination</b>:
      ${(scenario2.pC*100).toFixed(0)}% (${edgeC >= 0 ? "+" : ""}${edgeC.toFixed(0)} pts), because
      model and botanist err independently. Against a real baseline, a good model earns a
      few points — not a miracle.`;
  } else {
    cls = "lose";
    msg = html`At AUC-PR <b>${prauc2.toFixed(2)}</b> the SDM is <b>worse than the expert</b>
      (${(scenario2.pM*100).toFixed(0)}% vs ${(scenario2.pE*100).toFixed(0)}%) — a weak habitat
      model trails seasoned judgment. Even here, blending the two (${(scenario2.pC*100).toFixed(0)}%)
      claws back some ground. This is the finding DCA exists to surface: sometimes the model
      shouldn't drive the decision at all.`;
  }
  return htl.html`<div class="verdict ${cls}">${msg}</div>`;
}
```
